4. Autonomous — the system changes its own rules inside limits someone set. Exceptions go to a person.

→ Take last week. Your SDR was out sick all five days. What happened?
→ Name the document that decided which accounts got worked. Who owns it? When did it last change?

# Narrative Templates

## Portfolio scope: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound

The portfolio supports three distinct stories: graph8 connects the system; CIENCE helps operate the motion; Tenbound helps diagnose what needs to change. A Tenbound narrative starts with an unresolved pipeline constraint, uses the Standard or Maturity Model to frame the question, and explains what the Blueprint assessment delivers. End with an informed decision and next-step options. Do not invent a customer transformation or assume that the story must end in a graph8 or CIENCE purchase.

---

# Narrative Templates

**Brand Origin Story:** The problem was hiding in plain sight for anyone who had ever tried to run a B2B sales team at scale: the tools that were supposed to make revenue predictable had instead made it fragile. By the early 2020s, the average B2B go-to-market stack had ballooned to eight or more disconnected platforms — one for data, one for intent signals, one for email sequencing, another for dialing, a CRM that never quite reflected reality, a separate tool for quotes, another for e-signatures, and a spreadsheet for the forecast. Each charged per seat. Each required its own integration. Each held a fragment of the truth about a buyer. And none of them talked to each other in real time.

The founders of graph8 had spent a decade watching this problem compound through the lens of CIENCE, the managed B2B outbound firm that had run campaigns for more than 2,500 companies — from early-stage SaaS to Okta, Microsoft, Google, and Salesforce. CIENCE had accumulated something rare: millions of real conversations, calls, email replies, meeting dispositions, and pipeline outcomes across industries. They knew, at a granular level, which signals actually predicted buyer readiness, which messages actually got replies, and which handoffs between systems caused pipeline to disappear. They had seen the same problem from the inside of hundreds of revenue orgs: the data was scattered, the signals were siloed, and the people carrying information between tools by hand were the invisible load-bearing walls of every GTM motion.

The key insight was simple but radical: buyer data, intent signals, campaign execution, AI automation, CRM, and team collaboration should not be eight products. They should be one graph — a single, live record of every buyer, every signal, every conversation, and every deal, with every system reading from and writing to the same source of truth. And that graph should be free to search, with cost tied only to execution — what the system actually does, not how many people look at it.

graph8 was founded in 2024 to build that graph. Within its first year, it launched a platform that unified 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies in a searchable, always-enriched buyer graph; a signal engine that processes 2 billion buying signals daily across eight signal types and resolves each to a real person; a five-channel campaign sequencer covering email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp; AI voice agents that clone rep voices for inbound and outbound calls; an AI inbox that triages and drafts replies across every channel; a native CRM with deal management, quote-to-cash workflows, and revenue forecasting; a team collaboration workspace where AI agents and humans work in the same room; and Studio, an AI content engine that reads a company's website and generates 44 living strategy documents in one session.

At the same time, CIENCE continued running managed GTM execution for B2B teams that needed a team to run the motion, not just software to enable it. And Tenbound — the Pipeline Architecture Institute — published the Pipeline Architecture Standard and Programmable Revenue Blueprint: a six-pillar framework and a $1,000 three-week engineering-led assessment that maps every step of a revenue workflow before recommending a single tool.

Today, graph8 is the autonomous revenue system for B2B teams who are done paying a data tax, a seat tax, and a tool tax to eight vendors whose products were never designed to connect. The full platform runs for $99 per month for an entire organization — unlimited users, no seat fees, no annual contract. CIENCE manages GTM execution from $5,600 per month. And Tenbound's Programmable Revenue Blueprint gives any revenue leader a rigorous map of their pipeline system for $1,000. Together, these three offerings serve companies across the full spectrum: from self-serve platform users who want to search 700M contacts free, to fully managed execution clients who want a team running their motion, to revenue leaders who need an engineering-led diagnosis before they commit to scale.

The vision is a B2B revenue world where every buyer signal — from an anonymous site visit to a job-change alert to a social post — resolves instantly to a real person, triggers the right motion automatically, and flows through to closed revenue without a human carrying data between tools. Where the pipeline maturity ladder from Manual to Autonomous is something every team can climb with a published standard, a rigorous assessment, and a platform designed from the ground up to execute rather than observe. Where 'one graph, signal to revenue' is not a tagline but an operational fact.

**Brand Mission Narrative:** graph8 exists because the way B2B revenue teams work today is fundamentally broken — not for lack of effort, but for lack of a system. Revenue leaders are accountable for a number that depends on six interconnected pillars: the right market, the right signals, the right message, the right motion, the mastery to coach it, and the measurement to improve it. Most teams can only prove two or three of those pillars on any given quarter. The rest are held together by people carrying information between tools by hand, definitions that live in someone's head, and forecasts that are stale before Monday's pipeline call.

graph8's mission is to replace that fragmentation with one autonomous revenue system — a single buyer graph that connects data, signals, campaigns, AI agents, CRM, and human judgment so that every B2B team can build and close revenue without the operational drag of managing eight disconnected tools. The mission is not to add another SaaS product to the stack. It is to be the last layer the stack needs.

The change graph8 seeks to create is specific: a world where the unit of B2B revenue work shifts from 'person moving data between tools' to 'AI executing on behalf of a person who controls the limits.' Where 'qualified' means one thing everywhere — in the CRM, in the sequencer, in the routing rules, and in the AI agent's instructions — because someone wrote it down once and every system reads from the same record. Where a revenue team at a 20-person company has access to the same buyer intelligence, signal detection, and autonomous execution capability as a team of 200 — because the pricing is based on what the system does, not how many people use it.

graph8 serves its customers across three distinct layers. The platform serves teams who want to run revenue themselves on the best available infrastructure — starting free, scaling to $99 per month for the entire organization, with every GTM application included, no seat fees, and no annual contract. CIENCE serves teams who need a managed team to run the motion — with setup sprints, ongoing campaign execution, SDR capacity at multiple performance levels, and revenue system builds by forward-deployed engineers. Tenbound serves revenue leaders who need to understand their system before they invest in it — with the Pipeline Architecture Standard published free for any team to use, and the Programmable Revenue Blueprint available for $1,000 as an engineering-led assessment that produces five documents a team keeps and can implement without buying anything else.

The mission connects all three: every service, every assessment, every agent, and every integration exists to move B2B teams from wherever they are on the maturity ladder — Manual, Assisted, Orchestrated, or Autonomous — one clear step closer to a revenue system that runs itself inside the limits humans set, and gets better from every outcome it observes.

## Story Frameworks

### The Broken Stack Story

**Name:** The Broken Stack Story
**Description:** A framework that starts by naming the exact dysfunction of a fragmented GTM stack — tool by tool, cost by cost, manual step by manual step — then reveals that the dysfunction is structural, not fixable by adding another tool, and introduces the unified buyer graph as the architectural shift that resolves it. This framework works because it meets prospects exactly where they are: overwhelmed, over-billed, and under-delivered.
**Structure:**
- Open with the exact stack the audience is running today (data tool, intent tool, sequencer, dialer, CRM, quotes, billing, forecast spreadsheet — eight tools, eight bills, eight login screens)
- Name the hidden cost: the person carrying data between them by hand, the record that goes stale on export, the forecast that is already wrong by Monday
- Reveal the structural truth: these tools were never designed to connect, and adding a ninth tool does not fix an architectural problem
- Introduce the insight: if every signal, contact, conversation, and deal lived on one record — one buyer graph — every system would read the same truth and every agent would act on the same data
- Show the new world: one platform, one graph, signals that resolve to real people, launches that start automatically, CRM that fills itself, reps who work the right deal fully briefed
- Anchor with proof: $99/month, unlimited users, ten years of CIENCE campaign data training the AI, 700M+ contacts searchable free

**When To Use:** Best for top-of-funnel content aimed at revenue leaders and RevOps practitioners who are actively managing tool sprawl. Highly effective in long-form landing pages, sales presentations, and thought-leadership articles where the reader has time to follow a diagnostic argument.
**Example:** A VP of Revenue at a 60-person SaaS company opens her laptop on Monday morning. She has six tabs open before her first coffee: ZoomInfo for the account list, 6sense for intent signals, Outreach for sequences, Gong to review Friday's calls, Salesforce for the pipeline, and a Google Sheet where someone pastes the forecast numbers every week. She pays seat fees on four of them. The data in each reflects a slightly different version of the same buyer. When her best SDR leaves, half the context leaves with him. graph8 is built for her: one graph where every signal resolves to a real person, every launch starts automatically, and the CRM fills itself from real activity — for $99 a month for her entire team.

### The Maturity Ladder

**Name:** The Maturity Ladder
**Description:** A framework grounded in Tenbound's Sales Pipeline Maturity Model — four levels from Manual to Autonomous — that positions the audience on a ladder they can climb. Rather than selling a product, this framework sells a direction of travel: every team is somewhere on the ladder, the position costs money, and the next level is achievable with one written decision rather than one software purchase. graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound are positioned as the infrastructure, execution, and assessment that power each rung.
**Structure:**
- Establish the ladder: Manual (nothing runs when your best person is out), Assisted (tools send but reps still carry data by hand), Orchestrated (written rules build the queue and run the sequences), Autonomous (the system changes its own rules inside limits you set)
- Help the audience place themselves: the two diagnostic questions — what happened last week when whoever runs outbound was out sick, and what document decided which accounts got worked
- Name the cost of their current level: Level 2 (Assisted) is the most expensive — you pay for tools and people moving data between them simultaneously
- Show what the next level requires: not a purchase, but a decision written down — who decides which accounts get worked, what counts as qualified, when a sequence stops
- Introduce the path: Tenbound's Programmable Revenue Blueprint to map the current state and identify the constraint, CIENCE to run the motion while the system matures, graph8 to execute at scale once the definitions are written
- Close with the invitation: start by scoring yourself, or book a call where an engineer will tell you which pillar is capping the number

**When To Use:** Best for mid-to-bottom-of-funnel content aimed at revenue leaders who are evaluating AI tools or planning headcount decisions. Highly effective in webinars, Tenbound research publications, discovery call conversations, and board-level pipeline presentations where the audience needs a framework, not a feature list.
**Example:** A Head of Sales Development at a 200-person B2B software company buys an AI writing tool, watches reply rates jump for six weeks, then plateau. She runs the same diagnostic she always runs: more emails, better subject lines. The real problem is that the AI is sending at an unranked list — accounts nobody scored, in an order nobody decided, with a qualified-meeting definition nobody wrote down. She is at Assisted maturity. The jump to Orchestrated costs her nothing but one document: which accounts get worked, in what order, owned by one named person in RevOps. That document is what Tenbound's Programmable Revenue Blueprint produces. That document is what graph8's agents run on. The level moves. The number follows.

### The Signal-to-Revenue Loop

**Name:** The Signal-to-Revenue Loop
**Description:** A framework that follows a single buying signal — an anonymous site visit, a job change alert, a social post — all the way from detection to closed revenue on one buyer graph. This narrative arc makes the abstract concept of 'autonomous revenue' concrete by showing the exact sequence of events graph8 orchestrates, the exact moment a human steps in, and the exact outcome that gets recorded and remembered for next time.
**Structure:**
- Start with the signal: a VP of Sales at an enterprise company visits the pricing page three times in one week, then searches 'CRM migration' on industry sites
- Show the resolution: graph8 resolves the anonymous traffic to the company, then to the person — Jordan Lee, VP Sales, Northwind — with firmographics, technographics, intent score 92, ICP fit 88
- Show the automatic launch: My Desk surfaces the signal ranked first in the day's queue, the SDR Agent drafts a personalized first touch in the rep's voice, the Chief of Staff logs the action and waits for approval
- Show the human moment: the rep approves the draft, edits the subject line, sends — the reply comes back, the AI Inbox triages it as 'interested, requesting pricing', drafts the response
- Show the pipeline motion: the Deal Agent builds the quote on the opportunity record, the AE wins the live call, billing provisions itself on e-signature, the deal closes
- Close with the memory: every outcome — the signal that started it, the message that got the reply, the conversation that won the close — writes back to the buyer graph and shapes the next launch

**When To Use:** Best for product demos, website homepage narratives, and sales presentations where the audience needs to see the full motion end-to-end rather than feature by feature. Particularly effective when the buyer is evaluating whether 'autonomous revenue' is real or marketing language.

The SDR Agent drafts a three-sentence opener in Maya's voice. Maya edits one word and approves. Jordan replies Thursday asking for a demo. **Description:** A framework that positions graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound as parties who have seen the inside of more revenue operations than any single company's team ever will — and who can therefore distinguish between what teams say they do and what they actually do. **When To Use:** Best for bottom-of-funnel conversion content, competitive comparison pages, and sales conversations where the prospect is actively comparing graph8 to existing tools or evaluating a stack consolidation. Particularly effective in ROI calculators and pricing page companion content.
**Example:** A 25-person sales team paying for Apollo at $149/user/month, Outreach at $100/user/month, and Salesforce at $75/user/month is spending $8,100 per month — $97,200 per year — on three tools that don't share the same contact record and require a RevOps analyst to keep their integrations alive. graph8's Team plan at $99/month covers the entire team: 700M+ contacts searchable free, five-channel sequencer, AI dialer with voice cloning, AI inbox, native CRM with quote-to-cash, and AI agents running the volume. ## Narrative Hooks

Most tools give you a topic feed with no person behind it, siloed in a dashboard you have to check manually. graph8 resolves every signal to the real person on the buyer graph and auto-launches the right motion — so your team gets the call, fully briefed, while the interest is live.
